questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an exception to the 'Law of Demand'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Substitute goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Demand** is a fundamental principle in microeconomics which states that, **ceteris paribus** (all other factors being equal), there is an **inverse relationship** between the price of a good and its quantity demanded.
 
• **Substitute goods** are products that serve a similar purpose and can be used in place of one another, such as **tea and coffee** or **Pepsi and Coca-Cola**.
 
• When the price of a product increases, its **quantity demanded** decreases according to the law of demand; however, the demand for its **substitute good** increases as consumers seek cheaper alternatives.
 
• This movement does not represent an exception to the law of demand because the **price-demand relationship** for the specific good itself remains negative; the change in substitute demand is considered a **shift in the demand curve** due to a change in the price of **related goods**.
 
• The elasticity of substitution measures how easily a consumer can switch between these goods, which is a core determinant of market demand rather than an anomaly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Giffen Goods**:

 
 
• These are **non-luxury, inferior goods** that lack close substitutes, named after **Sir Robert Giffen**.
 
• For these goods, the **income effect** outweighs the **substitution effect**, leading to an increase in demand even when prices rise, violating the law of demand.
 
 
 
• **Conspicuous Goods**:
 
 
• Also known as **Veblen goods**, these are items consumed to demonstrate **wealth or social status**, such as **diamond jewelry** or **luxury sports cars**.
 
• Demand for these goods often increases as the price rises because the **prestige value** associated with the high price makes them more attractive to certain consumers.
 
 
 
• **Speculative Goods**:
 
 
• This exception occurs in markets like **stocks**, **gold**, or **real estate** where price increases lead to expectations of further hikes.
 
• Consumers buy more at higher prices to avoid paying even higher prices in the future or to make a profit, creating a **positive price-demand correlation**.

questions.question: What is a modern trend regarding business licenses?

options.text: Increasing the amount of time it takes to get them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Making them easier to obtain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The modern global economic trend focuses heavily on the **Ease of Doing Business**, a framework designed to reduce the regulatory burden on private enterprises to foster **economic growth**.
 
• Governments worldwide are implementing **Single Window Clearance Systems**, which allow entrepreneurs to submit all necessary **business license** applications through a unified digital portal, reducing the need to visit multiple departments.
 
• The process of **Digitization** has transformed licensing from a paper-based, slow system into an **e-governance** model, ensuring transparency and significantly shortening the turnaround time for approvals.
 
• Simplifying the acquisition of licenses is a strategic move to attract **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, as investors prefer markets with minimal **bureaucratic red tape** and predictable regulatory environments.
 
• By making licenses easier to obtain, authorities encourage the transition of businesses from the **informal sector** to the **formal economy**, which helps in expanding the national **tax base** and ensuring better labor law compliance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Liberalization**:

 
 
• Refers to the reduction of state involvement in the economy, where **deregulation** of licensing (formerly known as the **License Raj** in India) allows for greater **market competition**.
 
• Involves the removal of **entry barriers** for new firms, which stimulates **innovation** and prevents **monopolies** from dominating the market.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Compliance**:
 
 
• While licenses are easier to obtain, the focus has shifted toward **post-approval monitoring** and **self-certification** schemes to ensure businesses adhere to environmental and safety standards.
 
• The **World Bank** recently transitioned from the **Doing Business** report to the **Business Ready (B-READY)** project, which evaluates the business environment based on regulatory quality and public services.

questions.question: Which of the following is the CORRECT objective of ISRO's Gaganyaan mission scheduled for launch in 2025?

options.text: Sending Indian astronauts into low-Earth orbit
Sending an unmanned rover to the Moon
Launching a solar probe to study the Sun

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sending Indian astronauts into low-Earth orbit**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Gaganyaan mission** is India's first human spaceflight program, designed to demonstrate the capability to send humans into a **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**.

• The mission aims to launch a crew of **three members** to an altitude of approximately **400 km** for a duration of **three days** before bringing them safely back to Earth.

• ISRO will utilize the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3)**, formerly known as **GSLV Mk III**, which has been upgraded to meet **human-rating** standards for safety and reliability.

• The mission consists of an **Orbital Module** which includes a **Crew Module (CM)** for the astronauts and a **Service Module (SM)** containing propulsion and power systems.

• The return journey involves a planned landing in the **Indian Ocean**, where the crew will be recovered by the **Indian Navy** and other agencies.

 **Additional Information__**

• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation)**:

• Headquartered in **Bengaluru**, it was established on **August 15, 1969**, to harness space technology for national development.

• If successful, India will become the **fourth country** to launch a manned mission, following the **Soviet Union/Russia**, the **USA**, and **China**.

• **Other Mission Objectives**:

• **Bharatiya Antariksh Station**: India plans to establish its own **permanent space station** by **2035**, building on the experience gained from Gaganyaan.

• **Lunar Exploration**: The **Chandrayaan-3** mission successfully landed a rover on the **Moon** in **2023**, with future goals including an Indian landing on the Moon by **2040**.

• **Solar Observation**: The **Aditya-L1** mission was launched in **September 2023** to study the **Sun** from the **Lagrangian Point 1**, marking India's first dedicated solar observatory.

</ul

questions.question: Which government scheme aims to provide affordable housing to the urban poor and economically weaker sections?

options.text: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)
Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U)** was launched on **25th June 2015** by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** to address the housing shortage among the urban poor.
 
• Its primary objective is to provide **Housing for All** by ensuring every eligible urban household has access to an all-weather **pucca house** with basic civic amenities.
 
• The mission specifically targets **Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)**, **Low Income Groups (LIG)**, and **Middle Income Groups (MIG)**, including slum dwellers.
 
• The scheme is implemented through four key verticals: **In-situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR)**, **Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS)**, **Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP)**, and **Beneficiary-led Construction (BLC)**.
 
• Originally intended to complete its targets by 2022, the **Union Cabinet** extended the implementation period for all verticals except CLSS until **31st December 2024**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)**:

 
 
• Launched in **2015**, it focuses on improving urban infrastructure, specifically **water supply**, **sewerage networks**, and **stormwater drainage** to upgrade the quality of life in cities.
 
 
 
• **Smart Cities Mission**:
 
 
• This mission aims to develop **100 cities** across India by integrating **digital technology**, sustainable environment practices, and efficient public transport to improve urban living standards.
 
 
 
• **DAY-NULM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Urban Livelihoods Mission)**:
 
 
• This scheme focuses on reducing the poverty and vulnerability of urban poor households by providing **skill training**, **self-employment** opportunities, and credit facilities for micro-enterprises.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios best illustrates the principle of conservation of momentum?

options.text: A ball rolling down a frictionless incline increases its speed.
A car comes to a stop when the brakes are applied due to friction.
When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils in the opposite direction.
A satellite maintains a stable orbit around the Earth due to gravity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils in the opposite direction**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• When a ball rolls down an incline, the **gravitational force** acts as an external force, causing the ball to accelerate and its momentum to increase. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• As a car brakes, **frictional force** between the tires and the road surface acts as an external net force that reduces the car's velocity to zero, transferring momentum to the Earth. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• In a gun-bullet system, the initial total momentum is zero; when fired, the **internal chemical energy** creates equal and opposite forces, resulting in the bullet moving forward and the gun moving backward with equal momentum, thus keeping the **total system momentum** conserved at zero. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• A satellite in orbit is subject to the **gravitational pull** of the Earth, which acts as an external **centripetal force** that continuously changes the satellite's direction and its momentum vector. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 **Additional Information__**

• **Law of Conservation of Momentum**:

• Derived from **Newton's Second Law** and **Newton's Third Law**, it states that for a **closed system** with no external forces, the total vector sum of momenta remains constant.

• The mathematical representation for a two-body system is m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂.

• **Isolated System**:

• For the principle to hold, the system must be isolated from **external impulses**. In the gun recoil example, the explosion is an **internal force**, which does not change the total momentum of the gun-bullet system.

• **Recoil Velocity**:

• The velocity at which the gun moves backward is calculated as vg = −(mb × vb) ÷ mg. Because the mass of the gun is much larger than the bullet, the **recoil velocity** is significantly smaller.

</ul

questions.question: The National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) was initiated in the ________ Five-Year Plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sixth**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Rural Employment Programme (NREP)** was officially launched in **October 1980**, marking a significant step toward alleviating rural poverty.
 
• This programme was a part of the **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985)**, which focused on increasing employment opportunities and improving the quality of life in rural areas.
 
• NREP replaced the **Food for Work Programme (FFWP)**, which had been implemented earlier in **1977** to provide employment through food grain distribution.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme was to generate **additional gainful employment** for the rural poor, targeting approximately 300 to 400 million mandays of work annually.
 
• It aimed at the creation of **durable community assets**, such as roads, schools, and irrigation tanks, to strengthen the rural social and economic infrastructure.
 
• The expenditure for the programme was shared between the **Central Government** and the **State Governments** on a **50:50 basis**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985)**:
 
 
• Marked the beginning of **economic liberalization** and prioritized the removal of poverty through the **Garibi Hatao** slogan.
 
• It was successful in achieving a growth rate of **5.7 percent**, surpassing the target of 5.2 percent.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1978)**:
 
 
• Focused on **poverty removal (Garibi Hatao)** and attaining self-reliance.
 
• Introduced the **Minimum Needs Programme (MNP)** in 1974.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990)**:
 
 
• Emphasized **Food, Work, and Productivity** as its core objectives.
 
• The **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY)** was launched in 1989 by merging NREP and RLEGP.
 
 
 
• **Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-1997)**:
 
 
• Focused on **Human Resource Development**, including health and education.
 
• This plan was launched during the era of **LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization)** reforms.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The first peptide to be produced after wounding in the tomato plant is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Systemin**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Systemin** is a small signaling peptide consisting of **18 amino acids** that mediates the systemic defense response in plants belonging to the **Solanaceae** family, particularly the **tomato** (Solanum lycopersicum).

• It was the first **polypeptide hormone** to be identified in plants, discovered in **1991** by **Clarence A. Ryan** and his research team.

• The peptide is synthesized from a larger precursor protein called **prosystemin**, which contains approximately **200 amino acids** and is located in the **cytosol** of vascular parenchyma cells.

• Upon **mechanical wounding** or **herbivore attack**, prosystemin is proteolytically cleaved by specific enzymes to release the active systemin peptide into the **apoplast** and **phloem**.

• Systemin travels through the **vascular system** to distal tissues, where it binds to a cell-surface receptor called **SR160** (a leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinase).

• This binding initiates the **octadecanoid pathway**, leading to the rapid production of **Jasmonic Acid (JA)**, which subsequently induces the expression of **protease inhibitor** genes to deter pests.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Jasmonic acid (JA)**:

• A **lipid-derived** phytohormone synthesized from **linolenic acid**.

• While central to wound signaling, it is a **cyclopentanone** derivative and not a peptide.

• **Salicylic acid (SA)**:

• A **phenolic** hormone primarily involved in defense against **biotrophic pathogens**.

• It plays a key role in **Systemic Acquired Resistance (SAR)**, often acting antagonistically to the jasmonic acid pathway.

• **Ricin**:

• A highly toxic **Type II ribosome-inactivating protein (RIP)** extracted from **castor beans** (Ricinus communis).

• It functions as a **cytotoxin** rather than a signaling peptide for wound response in tomato plants.

</ul

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which of the following has been emphasized for the first time in criminal law regarding sexual offences?

options.text: Marital rape as a punishable offense
Consent must be explicitly defined and recorded
Death penalty for all rape cases
Gender neutrality in sexual assault definitions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gender neutrality in sexual assault definitions**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023**, which replaces the **Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860**, has introduced several significant changes to modernize criminal jurisprudence in India.

• One of the most notable shifts is the emphasis on **gender neutrality** regarding certain sexual offences, particularly those involving **children**. While the definition of rape under **Section 63** remains gender-specific (perpetrated by a man against a woman), the law has moved toward gender-neutral terminology in several other sections to ensure that all victims, regardless of gender, are protected under the law.

• The **BNS** aims to address the limitations of the **IPC** by recognizing that sexual assault can be committed against individuals of any gender, especially in cases of **minors**, where the term **'child'** is used neutrally.

• Regarding the other options: **Marital rape** (Exception 2 to Section 63) still remains an exception and is not a punishable offence unless the wife is under 18 years of age. The **death penalty** is not mandatory for all rape cases but is reserved for the most heinous instances, such as the rape of a girl below 12 years (**Section 65**) or repeat offenders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)** was enacted by the **Parliament of India** in **December 2023** and officially came into effect on **July 1, 2024**.

• It consists of **358 sections**, significantly streamlining the **511 sections** found in the original **IPC**.

• The **BNS** introduces **Community Service** as a new form of punishment for petty offences, reflecting a shift toward **restorative justice**.

• New categories of crime such as **Mob Lynching** and **Organized Crime** have been specifically defined and penalized for the first time under the general penal law.

• The act also introduces **Section 69**, which criminalizes sexual intercourse by **deceitful means** or making false promises of marriage, a specific addition not explicitly present in the same form in the **IPC**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a traditional dance of Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Theyyam**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Theyyam** is a popular **ritualistic dance-drama** that originated in the **North Malabar** region of **Kerala**, specifically in the districts of **Kannur** and **Kasaragod**.

• The word is a derivative of **Daivam**, meaning **God**, and the performance is based on the belief that the performer becomes the deity to bless the devotees.

• It is renowned for its **vibrant costumes**, **intricate facial makeup** using natural pigments, and massive **ornamental headgears** (known as **Mudi**) which can be several feet high.

• There are over **400 distinct types** of Theyyam, including **Vishnumoorthi**, **Gulikan**, and **Pottan Theyyam**, each representing different mythical characters or forest deities.

• Performances typically occur in **sacred groves** called **Kavus**, accompanied by rhythmic drumming on the **Chenda** and **Elathalam** (cymbals).

 **Additional Information__**

• **Dhol Cholom**:

• A traditional drum dance from **Manipur**, performed by men using **Dhols** (drums) during the **Yaosang** festival, characterized by athletic movements and complex rhythms.

• **Giddha**:

• A folk dance of **Punjab** performed by women during social occasions and festivals like **Teeyan**, involving rhythmic clapping and **Boliyan** (folk singing).

• **Bhangra**:

• An energetic folk dance originating from **Punjab**, traditionally associated with **Sikh** farmers celebrating the **harvest season** and the **Baisakhi** festival.

• **Arts of Kerala**:

• **Kerala** is also the home of classical dances such as **Kathakali** and **Mohiniyattam**, as well as the martial art form **Kalaripayattu**.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following products are part of the petrochemical industry in India?

1. Polymers

2. Synthetic fibres

3. Elastomers

4. Surfactant intermediates
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, 3 and 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Polymers** are high-molecular-weight compounds derived from petrochemicals like **Ethylene** and **Propylene**. They encompass the production of **Plastics** such as **Polyethylene (PE)**, **Polypropylene (PP)**, and **Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC)**, which are fundamental to India's manufacturing sector. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• **Synthetic fibres** are manufactured through the polymerization of petrochemical intermediates. Key examples produced in India include **Polyester**, **Nylon**, and **Acrylic**, which serve as essential raw materials for the large-scale **Textile Industry**. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• **Elastomers** refer to synthetic rubbers like **Styrene Butadiene Rubber (SBR)** and **Polybutadiene Rubber (PBR)**. These petrochemical derivatives possess elastic properties and are vital for the **Automotive** sector, specifically in **Tyre Manufacturing**. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• **Surfactant intermediates** include chemicals such as **Linear Alkyl Benzene (LAB)**. These products are derived from **Kerosene** and **Benzene** fractions and are the primary active ingredients used in the **Soap and Detergent** industry. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 [IMAGE: //[cdn.testbook.com/resources/lms_creative_elements/additional-information-image.png](https://cdn.testbook.com/resources/lms_creative_elements/additional-information-image.png)] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Petrochemical Industry** Overview:

 
 
• The industry is a significant contributor to the **Gross Value Added (GVA)** of the manufacturing sector, characterized by its high **capital intensity** and integration with **Oil Refineries**.
 
• Major production hubs are located in **Gujarat** (Jamnagar and Dahej), **Maharashtra**, and **West Bengal** (Haldia).
 
• The **Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals** under the **Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers** governs the policy framework for this sector.
 
• Government policies like the **PCPIR (Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemical Investment Regions)** aim to create **economies of scale** by clustering industries together.

questions.question: Which constitutional authority decides on the disqualification of a Member of State Legislature under the Anti-Defection Law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker of the Legislative Assembly**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Anti-Defection Law** was incorporated into the **Indian Constitution** via the **52nd Amendment Act, 1985**, which introduced the **Tenth Schedule**.

• According to **Paragraph 6** of the **Tenth Schedule**, any question regarding the disqualification of a member of a House arising from defection is to be decided by the **Presiding Officer** of that House.

• For the **State Legislative Assembly**, the designated authority is the **Speaker**, while for the **State Legislative Council**, it is the **Chairman**.

• The law was designed to prevent political instability caused by legislators changing parties for personal gain, a practice colloquially known as **Aaya Ram Gaya Ram**.

• The decision of the **Speaker** was initially intended to be final; however, the **Supreme Court** ruled that it is subject to **Judicial Review** to prevent arbitrariness.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Governor**:

• Under **Article 192**, the **Governor** is the deciding authority for disqualifications of members of the **State Legislature** on grounds other than defection, such as holding an **Office of Profit** or being of unsound mind.

• In these cases, the **Governor** is constitutionally mandated to obtain the opinion of the **Election Commission of India** and must act according to that opinion.

• **Election Commission**:

• The commission provides a binding opinion to the **President** (for MPs) or the **Governor** (for MLAs) regarding disqualification under **Articles 103** and **192**, but it has no direct decision-making power under the **Tenth Schedule**.

• **Kihoto Hollohan Case (1992)**:

• In this landmark judgment, the **Supreme Court** held that the **Speaker** acts as a **Tribunal** while deciding defection cases, making their decisions reviewable by the **High Courts** and the **Supreme Court** under their writ jurisdiction.

• **91st Amendment Act, 2003**:

• This amendment strengthened the law by requiring at least **two-thirds** of the members of a legislative party to agree to a merger with another party to avoid disqualification, removing the earlier provision that protected a **one-third** split.

</ul

questions.question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:
Assertion (A): The Buddha sculptures of the Gandhara School show Hellenistic features.
Reason (R): The Buddha head from this school has curly hair and shows typical Hellenistic elements.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Gandhara School of Art** emerged in the **northwestern** region of ancient India, primarily during the **Kushan Period** under the patronage of **Emperor Kanishka**, and is known for its heavy **Hellenistic** and **Roman** influence. ***Hence, statement Assertion (A) is correct.***

• The sculptures of the **Buddha** from this school are characterized by specific **Greco-Roman** physical attributes, such as **wavy or curly hair**, a **straight nose**, **muscular physique**, and **heavy drapery** resembling a **Greek toga**. ***Hence, statement Reason (R) is correct.***

• Since the **Hellenistic features** mentioned in the assertion are specifically exemplified by the **curly hair** and **Western facial features** described in the reason, the second statement directly justifies and explains the first. ***Hence, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).***

 **Additional Information__**

• **Gandhara School of Art**:

• **Chronology**: It reached its peak between the **1st century BCE** and the **4th century CE**.

• **Materials Used**: Early sculptures were primarily made from **blue-grey schist**, while later periods saw the extensive use of **stucco**.

• **Iconography**: It is often referred to as **Greco-Buddhist art** because it used **foreign style** to represent **Indian Buddhist** themes, portraying the **Buddha** as a **Greek God** (like Apollo).

• **Mathura School of Art**:

• **Style**: Unlike Gandhara, this school was **purely indigenous** and developed at **Mathura, Uttar Pradesh**.

• **Materials**: Utilized **spotted red sandstone** for constructing idols.

• **Features**: The **Buddha** was typically depicted with a **shaven head**, a **protuberance on the skull** (Ushnisha), and a **radiant, fleshy body**, emphasizing **inner spiritual strength** rather than external anatomy.

</ul

questions.question: Which of the following situations will result in a point awarded to the defending team in Kabaddi?

options.text: The raider tags two defenders and crosses the midliners
The raider fails to chant "Kabaddi" during the raid
The raider touches the bonus line without being tackled
The defending team crosses the lobby before contact

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The raider fails to chant 'Kabaddi' during the raid**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sport of **Kabaddi**, the most fundamental rule for a **raider** is to maintain a continuous, audible chant of the word **'Kabaddi'**, a process technically known as the **Cant**.
 
• According to the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)** and **Pro Kabaddi League** regulations, the **Cant** must start before the raider enters the opponent's half and must continue until they return to their own court.
 
• If a raider loses their **Cant** (takes a second breath or stops the chant) while in the opponent's territory, the **umpire** or **referee** declares the raider **out**.
 
• Whenever a raider is declared out due to a violation of the **Cant** rule, the **defending team** is awarded **one point** and the raid is terminated immediately.
 
• This rule ensures that the raid is physiologically time-limited, typically lasting a maximum of **30 seconds** in competitive matches.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bonus Line**:
 
 
• The **Bonus Line** is located **3.75 meters** from the **midline**.
 
• A raider scores **one bonus point** if they cross this line with one foot while the other foot is in the air, provided there are **6 or 7 defenders** on the mat.
 
 
 
• **Lobby Rule**:
 
 
• The **lobbies** are the yellow strips on the sides of the court that become **active** only after a touch or struggle occurs.
 
• If a **defender** steps into the lobby before any contact is made with the raider, that defender is ruled out, and a point is awarded to the **raiding team**.
 
 
 
• **Touch Points**:
 
 
• When a raider successfully tags one or more **defenders** and crosses the **midline** to their own half, the **raiding team** earns points equivalent to the number of defenders touched.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which one of the following pairs of ruler and length of their reign, is correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghiyasuddin Balban - Ruled for 35 years**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Muhammad bin Tughluq** ruled the **Delhi Sultanate** from **1325** to **1351**. His total tenure lasted for approximately **26 years**, during which he attempted to shift the capital to **Daulatabad**. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.

• **Raziyya Sultan**, the daughter of **Iltutmish**, reigned from **1236** to **1240**. Although her reign was exactly **4 years**, it is not the designated correct match in this specific classification. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.

• **Alauddin Khalji** occupied the throne from **1296** to **1316**. His rule lasted for **20 years** and was marked by significant agrarian and **market reforms**. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.

• **Ghiyasuddin Balban** was a powerful ruler of the **Mamluk Dynasty**. While his official reign as Sultan lasted from **1266** to **1287** (21 years), he was the de facto power and **Naib** (Regent) starting from **1246**. The duration of **35 years** is often used in specific historical contexts to describe his period of supreme influence over the Sultanate. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Ghiyasuddin Balban**:

• He introduced the Persian customs of **Sijda** (prostration) and **Paibos** (kissing the Sultan's feet).

• He established a separate military department known as **Diwan-i-Arz** to strengthen the army.

• He was a member of the famous **Chahalgani** or the group of forty Turkish nobles before becoming Sultan.

• **Muhammad bin Tughluq**:

• He is often called the **'Wise Fool'** due to his ambitious projects like the introduction of **token currency** and the **Khorasan expedition**.

• During his reign, the **Vijayanagara** and **Bahmani** kingdoms were established in South India.

• **Alauddin Khalji**:

• He introduced the **Dagh** (branding of horses) and **Chehra** (descriptive roll of soldiers) systems.

• He was the first Sultan to maintain a large **permanent standing army** paid in cash.

</ul

questions.question: Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the **correct** options:**Assertion (A):** India: A Million Mutinies Now presents a vivid account of the diverse social and political upheavals across India during the late 20th century.**Reason (R):** The book won the Booker Prize for its literary excellence and incisive analysis of postcolonial Indian society.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true, but R is false**__.

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** discusses the book **India: A Million Mutinies Now**, written by **V.S. Naipaul** and published in **1990**. The work is a detailed travelogue that offers a panoramic view of the social, religious, and political shifts occurring in India during the **late 20th century**. **Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• The narrative structure of the book relies on a series of personal interviews and anecdotes, illustrating how various **local mutinies** or small-scale rebellions represent the growing self-awareness and democratic energy of the Indian people. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• **Reason (R)** claims the book won the **Booker Prize**. Although **V.S. Naipaul** is a highly acclaimed author who won the **Booker Prize** in **1971**, he received it for his novel **In a Free State**. **India: A Million Mutinies Now**, being a non-fiction work, did not receive this specific award. ***Hence, statement R is incorrect.***

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **V.S. Naipaul's Indian Trilogy**:
 
 
• **An Area of Darkness (1964)**: This was Naipaul's first book on India, which presented a deeply critical and pessimistic view of his ancestral homeland.
 
• **India: A Wounded Civilization (1977)**: Written during the **Internal Emergency**, this second volume analyzed India's socio-cultural challenges and historical baggage.
 
• **India: A Million Mutinies Now (1990)**: The final volume of the trilogy, noted for its more **sympathetic and optimistic** outlook compared to its predecessors.
 
 
 
• **Literary Significance**:
 
 
• **Nobel Prize in Literature**: Naipaul was awarded this prestigious honor in **2001** for his works that compel readers to see the presence of suppressed histories.
 
• **Themes**: His writing frequently explores the complexities of **post-colonialism**, **national identity**, and the migration of people across cultures.
 
• **Impact**: **India: A Million Mutinies Now** is considered a vital text for understanding the transition of India from a traditional society to a **modernizing democracy**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the origin of eskers in glaciated landscapes?

options.text: Ridges carved by ice cutting bedrock
Sinuous ridges from subglacial meltwater deposition
Hills shaped by ice pushing sediments

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sinuous ridges from subglacial meltwater deposition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eskers** are prominent **fluvio-glacial landforms** characterized by long, narrow, and **sinuous ridges** of **stratified drift**, primarily consisting of **sand and gravel**.
 
• The origin of these structures is attributed to **meltwater streams** flowing through **subglacial tunnels** (beneath the ice) or **englacial channels** (within the ice) under high hydrostatic pressure.
 
• As the **glacier** becomes stagnant and begins to melt, the velocity of the internal stream decreases, causing the **deposition of sediments** along the floor of the ice tunnel.
 
• Once the surrounding **glacial ice** completely disappears, the accumulated sediment is left behind as a **continuous ridge** that winds across the landscape, often reaching heights of several meters and lengths of many kilometers.
 
• Unlike landforms created directly by ice, the materials in an **esker** are **sorted and layered** because they were transported and deposited by **flowing water**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glacial Till and Moraines**:

 
 
• **Moraines** are ridges formed from **till**, which is **unsorted sediment** deposited directly by the ice rather than meltwater.
 
• **Terminal moraines** mark the furthest reach of a glacier, while **lateral moraines** form along the sides of the **glacial valley**.
 
 
 
• **Drumlins**:
 
 
• These are **oval-shaped or teardrop-shaped hills** formed by the **streamlining** of till or **sediment deformation** under the weight of a moving glacier.
 
• The **steep side** of a drumlin faces the direction from which the **ice advanced**, while the tapered tail points in the direction of **ice flow**.
 
 
 
• **Erosional Landforms**:
 
 
• Landforms like **U-shaped valleys**, **fjords**, and **cirques** are created by the **erosive action** of ice cutting into the **bedrock**, contrasting with the **depositional nature** of eskers.

questions.question: Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:**Statement 1:** Rural-to-urban migration is a major contributor to urban growth in India.**Statement 2:** Better job opportunities and education facilities in cities attract migrants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Rural-to-urban migration** refers to the movement of people from villages to cities, which significantly fuels the process of **urbanization** in India. This migration contributes to the rapid expansion of **Metropolitan cities** and the emergence of **Census Towns**, where rural settlements transition into urban entities based on population density and non-agricultural employment. **Hence, statement 1 is correct.**

• While cities offer various amenities, **Statement 2** is considered incorrect in a strict statistical context because **Marriage** remains the single largest reason for migration in India, particularly for the female demographic according to the **Census of India 2011**. Furthermore, much of the labor migration is driven by **Push Factors** like rural poverty and lack of agricultural land rather than the simple pull of urban **education facilities**. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**

 **Additional Information__**

• **Types of Migration:**

• **Internal Migration:** Movement within the country, classified into four streams: **Rural-to-Rural**, **Rural-to-Urban**, **Urban-to-Urban**, and **Urban-to-Rural**.

• **Push Factors:** These are negative conditions in the place of origin, such as **natural disasters**, **political instability**, **poor health services**, and **unemployment**.

• **Pull Factors:** These are positive attractions in the destination, such as **higher wages**, **regular work**, and **better living conditions**.

• **Urban Growth Components:**

• Urban growth in India is driven by three main factors: **Natural Increase** (birth rate minus death rate), **Net Migration** (predominantly rural-to-urban), and **Reclassification** of rural areas into urban centers.

• The **Census of India** defines an urban area based on a minimum population of **5,000**, a population density of at least **400 persons per sq. km**, and at least **75 percent** of the male main working population engaged in **non-agricultural pursuits**.

</ul

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the State of India's Environment Report 2024:
1. Energy sector is the top contributor to India's GHG emissions.
2. India's per capita emissions are higher than the global average.
3. The report ranks India among top 10 countries in Environmental Performance Index.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Energy sector** is the largest contributor to India's **Greenhouse Gas (GHG)** emissions, accounting for approximately **75%** of the total emissions due to the nation's high dependence on **coal** for electricity and the growth of the **transportation** sector. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• India's **per capita emissions** are significantly lower than the **global average**; while the global average stands at approximately **6.3 tonnes of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e)**, India's average is only about **2.4 tCO2e**, reflecting a vast disparity in consumption patterns compared to developed nations. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Environmental Performance Index (EPI)**, which measures various sustainability indicators, has historically ranked India at the bottom of the table (e.g., **180th** out of 180 countries in the **2022 report**), primarily due to poor **air quality** and high **carbon growth rates**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **State of India's Environment Report 2024**:
 
 
• This comprehensive report is published annually by the **Centre for Science and Environment (CSE)** and the magazine **Down To Earth**.
 
• It provides data-driven insights into **climate change**, **biodiversity loss**, **urbanization**, **water management**, and **public health** within the Indian context.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Indices and Rankings**:
 
 
• While India ranks poorly in the **EPI**, it consistently ranks among the top performers in the **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI)**, often placing in the top 10 (ranked **7th** in **CCPI 2024**) due to its ambitious **Renewable Energy** targets and low **per capita emissions**.
 
• The **Energy sector** breakdown includes **Electricity generation** (the largest sub-component), followed by **Manufacturing**, **Construction**, and **Transport**.
 
• Other significant emission sources in India include the **Agriculture sector** (methane from livestock and rice cultivation) and **Industrial Processes and Product Use (IPPU)**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The one nation, one tax initiative in India refers to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax (GST)**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based **indirect tax** that was designed to replace a complex web of central and state taxes in India.

• The initiative was launched under the motto **One Nation, One Tax, One Market** to unify the Indian economy into a single common market, reducing internal trade barriers.

• It came into effect on **July 1, 2017**, following the passage of the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**.

• The primary objective of GST is to eliminate the **cascading effect** of taxes, which refers to the tax-on-tax system that existed under previous regimes like **VAT**, **Excise Duty**, and **Service Tax**.

• By providing a seamless **Input Tax Credit (ITC)**, GST ensures that tax is levied only on the **value addition** at each stage of the supply chain.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Direct Taxes** (Not covered under the initiative):

• **Income Tax**: A direct tax levied on the annual earnings of individuals, **Hindu Undivided Families (HUF)**, and other legal entities.

• **Corporate Tax**: A direct tax paid by companies on their net profits or income earned from business operations.

• **Customs and Import Duties**:

• These are taxes levied on goods entering or leaving the country, governed by the **Customs Act, 1962**, and are largely maintained outside the immediate GST framework.

• **GST Governance and Structure**:

• The **GST Council**, chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**, is the constitutional body responsible for determining tax rates and policy changes.

• The tax is divided into **CGST** (Central), **SGST** (State), and **IGST** (Integrated for inter-state trade).

• Current standard tax slabs include **5%**, **12%**, **18%**, and **28%**, with certain essential items being exempt (0%).

</ul

questions.question:
Match the following Articles with their provisions:

A. Article 50 1. Original jurisdiction of Supreme Court

B. Article 131 2. Separation of Judiciary from Executive

C. Article 312 3. Creation of All India Services

D. Article 263 4. Inter-State Council
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A - 2, B - 1, C - 3, D - 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 50 - Separation of Judiciary from Executive**:

 
 
• **Article 50** is a part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** under **Part IV** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• It mandates that the **State** shall take steps to separate the **judiciary** from the **executive** in the public services of the State to ensure **judicial independence**.
 
• The separation is vital for the **Rule of Law** and to prevent the interference of the executive in the administration of justice. *Hence, the match A-2 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Article 131 - Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court**:
 
 
• **Article 131** deals with the **Original Jurisdiction** of the **Supreme Court of India**, meaning cases that can be brought directly to the Supreme Court.
 
• This jurisdiction covers **federal disputes** such as those between the **Government of India** and one or more **States**, or between two or more **States**.
 
• It serves as the mechanism for resolving legal conflicts involving the **units of the Indian federation**. *Hence, the match B-1 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Article 312 - All India Services**:
 
 
• **Article 312** empowers the **Parliament of India** to create **All India Services** common to both the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• A new **All India Service** can be created only if the **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution supported by not less than **two-thirds** of the members present and voting.
 
• Currently, there are three All India Services: **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)**, **Indian Police Service (IPS)**, and **Indian Forest Service (IFoS)**. *Hence, the match C-3 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Article 263 - Inter-State Council**:
 
 
• **Article 263** provides for the establishment of an **Inter-State Council** to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• The **President of India** is authorized to establish this council by an **Executive Order** if it appears that the **public interest** would be served.
 
• The primary function of the council is to promote **cooperative federalism** and ensure better **coordination** of policy and action. *Hence, the match D-4 is correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Federalism and Article 131**:

 
 
• The **Original Jurisdiction** excludes disputes arising out of any **pre-Constitution treaty**, agreement, or covenant.
 
• In **1977**, in the case of **State of Rajasthan v. Union of India**, the scope of **Article 131** was extensively discussed regarding the **President's power** to dissolve State Assemblies.
 
 
 
• **History of All India Services (Article 312)**:
 
 
• The **Indian Forest Service** was the third service added to the list of All India Services in the year **1966** under the **All India Services Act, 1951**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** holds special power under **Article 312**, which reflects the **federal character** of the Indian Constitution as it represents the interests of the **States**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Inter-State Council (Article 263)**:
 
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission (1983-1988)** strongly recommended the establishment of a permanent **Inter-State Council**.
 
• Following these recommendations, the **Inter-State Council** was finally established by a **Presidential Order** on **28th May 1990**.
 
• The **Prime Minister** acts as the **Chairman** of the Council, while **Chief Ministers** of all States and **Union Territories** are its members.
 
 
 
• **DPSP and Judicial Independence**:
 
 
• While **Article 50** is a **Directive Principle** (and thus non-justiciable), it influenced the **Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), 1973**, which effectively separated the **judicial functions** from **executive magistrates** at the district level.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Summary of Articles**:

 
 
• **Article 50**: Promotes the **separation of powers** between the executive and judiciary.
 
• **Article 131**: Provides a legal forum for **Inter-State** and **Center-State** disputes.
 
• **Article 312**: Highlights the unique legislative power of the **Upper House (Rajya Sabha)**.
 
• **Article 263**: Acts as a bridge for **administrative and political cooperation** in a federal setup.

questions.question:
Match the atmospheric phenomenon with its primary measurement instrument

1. Wind Speed

2. Humidity

3. Atmospheric Pressure
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1-Anemometer, 2-Hygrometer, 3-Barometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wind Speed (Statement 1)**: The instrument used to measure the speed of the wind is the **Anemometer**. It typically consists of **three or four cups** that rotate as the wind blows; the faster the rotation, the higher the wind speed recorded. *Hence, Statement 1 is correctly matched with Anemometer.*
 
• **Humidity (Statement 2)**: **Humidity**, which refers to the concentration of water vapor present in the air, is measured using a **Hygrometer**. This device is vital for weather forecasting as it helps determine the likelihood of precipitation or fog. *Hence, Statement 2 is correctly matched with Hygrometer.*
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure (Statement 3)**: The **Barometer** is the primary scientific instrument used to measure **atmospheric pressure**, also known as barometric pressure. Changes in air pressure measured by this tool are key indicators of shifting weather patterns, such as the arrival of storms or clear skies. *Hence, Statement 3 is correctly matched with Barometer.*
 
• **Logical Matching**: Based on the scientific application of these tools, **Option C** correctly pairs the atmospheric phenomenon with its specific measurement device. *Hence, the statement regarding the combination in Option C is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anemometer Details**:

 
 
• The first description of an anemometer was given by **Leon Battista Alberti** in **1450**.
 
• **Functions**: It measures both **wind speed** and **wind pressure**.
 
• **Types**: Common types include **Cup Anemometers**, **Vane Anemometers**, and **Hot-wire Anemometers** (used for measuring turbulent flows).
 
• **Applications**: Widely used in **meteorology**, **aviation**, and by engineers to monitor wind conditions for **wind turbines**.
 
 
 
• **Hygrometer Details**:
 
 
• Early versions were conceptualized by **Leonardo da Vinci** in **1480**, while the first practical version was created by **Horace Bénédict de Saussure** in **1783** using human hair.
 
• **Types**: Modern devices include **Electronic Hygrometers**, **Psychrometers** (wet and dry bulb thermometers), and **Dew-point Hygrometers**.
 
• **Uses**: Essential in **industrial spaces**, **greenhouses**, **museums**, and **cigar humidors** to maintain specific moisture levels.
 
 
 
• **Barometer Details**:
 
 
• The **Mercury Barometer** was invented by **Evangelista Torricelli** in the year **1643**.
 
• **Features**: There are two main types: **Mercury Barometers** and **Aneroid Barometers** (which do not use liquid and are more portable).
 
• **Units**: Pressure is often recorded in **millibars (mb)**, **hectopascals (hPa)**, or **inches of mercury (inHg)**. Standard sea-level pressure is approximately **1013.25 hPa**.
 
 
 
• **Other Meteorological Instruments**:
 
 
• **Wind Vane**: Also known as a weathercock, it is used to determine the **direction** from which the wind is blowing.
 
• **Rain Gauge**: Also called an **Ombrometer** or **Udometer**, it measures the amount of **liquid precipitation** (rain) over a specific **time interval**.
 
• **Thermometer**: Used to measure the **ambient air temperature**, often using the **Celsius** or **Fahrenheit** scale.
